subject: geography
title: Depressions, Anticyclones & Symbols
welcome_lead: Why does the weather change? Learn about depressions, anticyclones, and how to read a weather map.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on depressions, anticyclones and weather map symbols.
final_note: Brilliant! You can now read a basic weather forecast.

concepts.def: Area of low pressure bringing wet, windy weather.
Area of high pressure bringing calm, dry weather.
Boundary between warm and cold air masses.
Line on a map joining points of equal pressure.
Warm air rising over cold air, bringing rain.
Cold air pushing under warm air, heavy showers.

walkthroughs.body_html: Depressions have low pressure at their centre. They bring cloud, rain and wind. The UK gets many in winter from the Atlantic.
Anticyclones have high pressure. They bring clear skies, calm winds and sunny weather — or frost in winter.
Curved lines are isobars. Close isobars = strong winds. Blue triangles = cold front. Red semicircles = warm front.
